Stephanie Hodges · “Moonflower” · Seamstress & Wardrobe

The hands behind the wardrobe.

I'm Stephanie — a seamstress who works where the music is. Backstage, I keep performers stage-ready: steaming, pressing, sewing, and fixing whatever the night throws at a garment. In the studio, I alter, repair, and build original pieces by hand — including the headdresses I make and teach.

If you got this link from me, this is the good stuff: what I can do, the work I'm known for, and how to book me or claim an original piece.

What I do

Four ways to hire the needle — from a single torn seam five minutes before showtime to a one-of-a-kind piece built from scratch.

01

Backstage Wardrobe & Show-Day Support

Wardrobe and seamstress support for live music and events. I prep the rack before doors, keep garments pressed and ready through the show, and handle the emergencies — a split seam, a lost button, a zipper that quits at soundcheck. In May 2026 I provided wardrobe and seamstress support for Cardi B: steaming, ironing, and sewing.

Steaming & pressing Quick repairs Rack prep Show-day dressing support
02

Alterations & Repairs

The everyday magic: clothes that fit like they were made for you, and favorites brought back from the brink. Bring me the dress that almost fits, the jacket with the torn lining, the jeans you've loved to death.

Hems & tailoring Fit adjustments Mending & patching Buttons, zippers & linings
03

Custom & Original Pieces

One-of-a-kind garments and pieces made to order — designed with you, built by hand, and finished to be worn on stage, at a festival, or anywhere you want to arrive as yourself. Originals are sold through my Rising Moon Products line.

Custom clothing Stage & festival wear One-of-a-kind originals Jewelry & artwork
04

Headdresses & Classes

My signature work. I build ornate handmade headdresses — moons, feathers, beadwork, and 3D-printed elements — and I teach classes where you build your own. Class kits with the printed parts are part of the deal: you get your kit through me, and class day is assembly, hand-finishing, and making it unmistakably yours.

Finished headdresses Commissions Hands-on classes 3D-printed part kits

Good questions

          

          

            Can you handle a show-day emergency?
            
That's the job. Backstage work is mostly emergencies handled calmly — split seams, dead zippers, last-minute fit problems. If you're booking wardrobe support for an event, tell me the date and the size of the act in the builder above.

          

          

            How do headdress classes work?
            
You book a seat, and your class kit — including the 3D-printed parts for that design — comes through me as part of the deal, so everything you need is waiting for you. Class day is assembly plus the hand work: fitting, finishing, and making the piece yours.

          

          

            Do you take commissions?
            
Yes — custom clothing, headdresses, jewelry, and artwork. Commissions start with a conversation about what you want, your timeline, and your budget; I'll tell you straight whether I'm the right hands for it.

          

          

            How fast can alterations be done?
            
It depends on the garment and the season — show season books up. Put your date in the request builder and I'll give you a real answer, not a guess.
